{{short description|Mathematical award}}
The '''Hausdorff medal''' is a mathematical prize awarded every two years by the European Set Theory Society. The award recognises the work considered to have had the most impact within [[set theory]] among all articles published in the previous five years. The award is named after the German mathematician [[Felix Hausdorff]] (1868–1942).

== Winners ==
*2013: [[W. Hugh Woodin|Hugh Woodin]] for his articles "Suitable extender models I"<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Woodin |first=Hugh |date=2010 |title=Suitable extender models, I |journal=[[Journal of Mathematical Logic]] |volume=10 |issue=2 |pages=101–339 |doi=10.1142/S021906131000095X}}</ref> and "Suitable extender models II: beyond ''ω''-huge".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Woodin |first=Hugh |date=2011 |title=Suitable extender models II: beyond ''ω''-huge |journal=Journal of Mathematical Logic |volume=11 |issue=2 |pages=115–436 |doi=10.1142/S021906131100102X}}</ref>
*2015: [[Ronald Jensen]] and [[John R. Steel|John Steel]] for their article "''K'' without the measurable".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Jensen |first=Ronald |last2=Steel |first2=John |date=2013 |title=''K'' without the measurable |journal=[[Journal of Symbolic Logic]] |volume=78 |issue=3 |pages=708–734 |jstor=43303677|doi=10.2178/jsl.7803020}}</ref>
*2017: [[Maryanthe Malliaris]] and [[Saharon Shelah]] for their article "General topology meets model theory, on 𝔭 and 𝔱".<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Malliaris |first=Maryanthe |last2=Shelah |first2=Saharon |date=2013 |title=General topology meets model theory, on 𝔭 and 𝔱 |url=https://www.pnas.org/doi/epdf/10.1073/pnas.1306114110 |journal=[[Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America]] |volume=110 |issue=33 |pages=13300–13305 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1306114110 |jstor=42712902|url-access=subscription }}</ref><ref name=3hm>{{cite web|title=Third Hausdorff Medal 2017|url=https://ests.wordpress.com/2017/07/05/third-hausdorff-medal-2017/|publisher=European Set Theory Society|date=July 5, 2017|access-date=2017-08-01}}</ref>
*2019: [[Itay Neeman]] for his work on "the new method of iterating forcing using side conditions and the tree property".<ref name="KGRC">{{cite web |title=The Hausdorff Lecture 2019: Itay Neeman - The tree property forcing axioms everywhere |url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=I63MosIci_o |website=YouTube |publisher=Kurt Gödel Research Center |accessdate=1 February 2020}}</ref>
*2022: [[David Asperó]] and [[Ralf Schindler]] for their positive solution to the long standing conjecture that MM++, a strong form of Martin’s Maximum, implies Woodin’s Axiom (*).<ref name="ESTS 2">[https://ests.wordpress.com/hausdorff-medals/ Award page at the website of the European Set Theory Society]</ref>
*2024: [[Gabriel Goldberg]] for his work on the Ultrapower Axiom, isolating abstract properties of inner models with supercompact cardinals.<ref name="spp2026">{{cite web |title=Hausdorff medal 2024 |url=https://blog.spp2026.de/hausdorff-medal-2024/ |publisher=SPP 2026 – Geometry at Infinity |date=September 18, 2024}}</ref>
